Page 1 of 4, 7 total items. Brian Tallerico RogerEbert.com Apr 13 Content collapsed. It’s not a typical hagiographic music doc in that it actually tears down as much as it elevates, revealing the insecurities, uncertainties, and even body dysmorphia of its subject. Go to Full Review Alfred Castaneda Shade Studios 3d Content collapsed. Far from being an all-too-common hagiographic portrait of a star, Kahan’s candidness leads to refreshingly emotional and touching moments that shape the man behind the lyrics. Go to Full Review Chris Joyce Movies and Munchies (YouTube) 4d Content collapsed. From self-effacing humor to tearful self-reflection, Noah demonstrates that fame isn’t always what it’s assumed to be, but it can also be used as a tool for good to encourage and inspire all to the beat of a melodic guitar strum. Go to Full Review Johnny Loftus Decider 5d Content collapsed. Noah Kahan offers a lighthearted look at his music career in Out of Body. But when he goes back home to Vermont, things get more thoughtful. Go to Full Review Belen Prieto Espinof Apr 15 Content collapsed. It's a documentary that both deconstructs and builds upon [Noah Kahan's] persona, and that's where its value lies. Compared with the stack of musician documentaries that have landed on the streaming market in recent years, this one is rawer and more open, making it more interesting.
